change: Nested walk-forward choices for test week w (change-rule parameters, path threshold, walk-forward P(change within 48 h) maps) now use only issues whose whole 48 h outcome was known at the start of week w (fra.changetime.known_before: issue + 48 h + KNOWN_LAG_H <= week start); the blend's walk-forward P48 map uses the features of week w's nested parameters, not the all-weeks choice. fra/changetime.py main, experiments/integration/nextchange.py, final_eval.py; data/changetime_eval.csv, nextchange_results.json, final_eval.json regenerated.
effect: out-of-sample next-change event accuracy restated: blend nested 0.802 -> 0.800, logit nested 0.779 -> 0.778; walk-forward P48 Brier logit 0.0586 -> 0.0646, blend 0.0629 -> 0.0686 (mostly less training data in the early weeks). Deployed parameters (BLEND_CHANGE_PARAMS, PARAMS, P48 coefficients) and every forecast unchanged.
why: independent review: the earlier nested masks let outcomes up to 50 h inside week w inform week w's parameters (small look-ahead)

change: fra.scoring computes the truth with fra.labels.to_labels(load_counts(), bridge="night") (the code used the default bridge "ffill", which also carries the OD across unfetched daytime hours); per window it reports valid hours observed / bridged / unlabelled.
effect: before the holdout, 1 hour since 1 Jun (2026-08-06 16 UTC) was labelled only by a daytime carry-over; no live hour affected so far
why: the registered text already said 'carried through the night ban and quiet hours'; the code now matches it

change: analysis.ci: 3-day blocks of the valid time (fra.evalkit.day_blocks(block_days=3); fra.scoring.BLOCK_DAYS) instead of 1-day blocks for every CI of the variant comparison incl. the decision rules D1-D3; the pooled Brier difference is also reported with 1- and 7-day blocks (sensitivity, not decisive).
why: daily paired Brier differences are autocorrelated (long test lag-1 0.21, lag-2 0.07, lag-3 0.09); with 1-day blocks D1/D2 would fire more often than nominal

topic: claims: no selection-free part for the blend
change: 'selection_free' renamed 'pre_sep15_part' in the integration outputs and here; champion_choice marked as decided at 17:35 UTC on the long test (in-sample) and documented afterwards; statement added that all of Jun-Oct 2026 was used to select the blend design and that only the holdout decides.
effect: no number changed; the blend's long-test gain is an in-sample upper bound
why: independent review: Part A / Part B defaults, anticipate='mean', the 50/50 weight and the change parameters were chosen on the whole long test

topic: new runtime 2026-10-31-wave2-r3 for blend-v2 and logit-v2 (before the holdout)
change: Forecast-module changes that do not change any forecast under normal operation: (a) a champion entry that cannot be resolved (import / attribute / signature error) is a model error -> next candidate at once; first fallback candidate = the champion's own logit with fra.predict (intention to treat: still blend-v2); (b) a served ECMWF / ICON single run is used only if it covers every hour the forecast needs, else the run one cycle earlier; every run used and every fallback is recorded in the issued .json (live_inputs) and runs.jsonl; (c) live METAR and second-NWP requests with (5, 30) s timeouts, the second NWP (not a feature of the production logit) NaN instead of failing the hour; (d) the Part B analogue library is read from a frozen read-only copy (data/archive/models/blend-v2/library/, MANIFEST.json sha256 d38e3f72b613, registry models.library + models_sha256 pin) instead of the live data/ files; (e) run records: package versions, registry sha256, a check of the forecast-module hashes against this registration; (f) corrected comments. logit-v1 and hackathon keep their runtimes.
effect: verified identical: the working-tree champion reproduced the official 18 UTC forecast exactly (p_od25, p_rwy18_open, logit and decision parts max |diff| 0.0) with the frozen library; smoke PASS for all four variants
why: independent review: silent fallbacks, unfrozen library inputs, an entry failure losing the hour

topic: job time :12 -> :30 local time; unit hardening; backup
change: fra-archive.timer OnCalendar *:30 (was *:12); the unit calls <repo>/.venv/bin/python directly (no `uv run`, which re-locks / re-syncs the shared environment at each start); a backup step copies data/archive, data/inaa_counts.csv and this file to ~/fra-archive-backup every hour (+ a daily sha256 manifest of the issued files).
effect: the od_now source hour [t-2h, t-1h) is read ~90 min after its end instead of ~72 min (it was complete in every measured hour after 75-79 min; at 72 min 2 of 3 measured hours still lacked 1-2 movements); ECMWF run init <= t-6h is read 6.5 h after init instead of 6.2 h. Issue hours and leads are unchanged (valid = issue + lead); logit-v1 / hackathon read their newest, partly published radar hour 18 min later than at :12.
why: independent review: residual train/serve skew of od_now / rwy18_now / west_frac_now and an IFS publication buffer on the edge

change: r4 = r3 with only fra/alerts.py replaced (ops.runtime snapshot --base 2026-10-31-wave2-r3 --files fra/alerts.py): a notification for official hours that were never issued (coverage gaps). blend-v2 and logit-v2 moved to r4; their forecast modules are byte-identical to r3.
